observed_mechanisms.observation: PlanOut random operators are deterministic functions of experiment salt, operator/variable salt and unit identity. The pinned Python implementation builds a salt-plus-unit string, hashes it with SHA-1, truncates the digest and derives deterministic integers/floats/choices from it.

Assignment automatically uses the assigned variable name as an operator salt when no explicit salt is supplied; tests verify that changing variable or assignment salt changes assignments while an explicit full salt can deliberately equalize assignments across Assignment objects.
SimpleNamespace allocates sampled segments from an available-segment set, removes allocated segments, maps each segment to one experiment name and deterministically maps a primary unit to a segment.

Experiment parameter access can lazily trigger a one-per-instance exposure log. The log binds experiment name, time, salt, inputs, assigned params and a source checksum; logging can also be made explicit/manual.

negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.finding: The SimpleNamespace documentation states that allocation state is not stored and is dependent on the full setup history; inserting earlier add/remove calls can move segments between experiments.
negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.f2_consequence: Do not transplant SimpleNamespace state or append-order semantics. F2 assignment must bind a versioned immutable experiment plan/assignment identity so later plan edits cannot silently reinterpret old units.

negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.finding: PlanOut auto-exposure can be emitted when a parameter is fetched; its own documentation distinguishes preparation/assignment from actual exposure and supports manual logging when the parameter may not yet affect the user.
negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.f2_consequence: Never map PlanOut exposure directly to WP507 UPTAKEN or causal influence. F2 must preserve ASSIGNED/OFFERED/DELIVERED/UPTAKEN/DOWNSTREAM_DELTA as separate evidence states.

negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.finding: The pinned runtime uses SHA-1 plus string concatenation and truncated digest arithmetic for deterministic randomization.
negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.f2_consequence: Reuse only deterministic domain separation. Do not adopt SHA-1/string concatenation as the F2 ABI. Use F2 canonical serialization plus an explicit digest algorithm/domain/version bound into the assignment receipt.

negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.finding: The pinned logging documentation describes an MD5 code checksum, while the pinned Python Experiment implementation computes a truncated SHA-1 checksum of assignment source/script.
negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.f2_consequence: Do not rely on prose labels for reproducibility identity. Bind exact source/artifact digest and algorithm in machine-readable receipts.

negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.finding: The upstream repository is archived and read-only.
negative_evidence_and_transfer_limits.f2_consequence: Reject direct runtime dependency adoption for this gate; concept distillation only.

f2_distillation.purpose: Generate a replay-stable assignment for WP507 matched intervention/control probes without becoming evidence or effect authority.
invariants: Same canonical assignment identity and version must replay to the same treatment class.
Changing experiment domain/version must deliberately change assignment identity rather than silently reinterpret prior evidence.
Mutually exclusive treatment classes must never overlap for one assignment identity.
Assignment is not delivery, uptake, downstream influence, world truth or effect success.
Assignment output is candidate experiment-control metadata only and cannot bypass UnifiedDB/evidence authority or EffectGate/EffectJournal.
Historical assignment receipts must remain interpretable after later experiment-plan edits.
f2_distillation.recommended_architecture_shape: Pure deterministic F2-native function plus immutable/versioned assignment receipt; no second mutable allocation database, no PlanOut runtime dependency, and no PlanOut exposure semantics imported into GWT evidence states.

hypothesis.statement: A versioned deterministic assignment primitive distilled from PlanOut's salt/unit namespace pattern can reduce allocation drift and treatment overlap in WP507 matched intervention/control tests while preserving F2 evidence authority boundaries.

counterhypotheses.statement: A direct fixed alternation or explicit caller-supplied treatment class is simpler and equally reproducible; hash/domain assignment adds no information.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: E3 fixture should compare replay stability, accidental overlap, order sensitivity and plan-edit behavior for explicit alternation versus a versioned canonical-digest assignment. If explicit assignment preserves all invariants with lower complexity, reject the digest allocator.

counterhypotheses.statement: Deterministic assignment can create hidden confounding if the unit identity or domain is correlated with downstream recipient behavior.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Use paired controls and assignment-balance diagnostics; treatment assignment alone must never be taken as causal proof.

counterhypotheses.statement: Namespace segmentation is unnecessary for the immediate two-run WP507 matched-pair gate and adds avoidable machinery.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Keep E3 scoped to a minimal pure assignment function; only add namespace allocation if concurrent/multi-treatment experiments demonstrate a concrete collision/isolation failure.

recommended_next_trigger6_objective.task: Build a source-equivalent deterministic fixture that reproduces the pinned PlanOut salt/unit assignment invariants, then compare them against a minimal F2-native canonical-digest assignment under replay, treatment-set reorder, plan-version change and historical-receipt re-entry. Do not grant WP507 causal or runtime credit from the fixture.
